note: How to replay trace.json against a port. Follow this exactly; a mismatched harness produces divergence that is not in the sim, which has already cost this project real time three separate times (see docs/DECISIONS.md on harness faults).

timestep.rule: ALWAYS step with exactly fixedDt. The sim is deterministic only at a fixed timestep; a variable frame time is a different simulation, not a faster one.

rng.rule: Course generation consumes the PRNG in a fixed order. Adding, removing or REORDERING a single R() call inside course generation changes every course from that point on. Derive values from existing draws instead of taking new ones.

input.policyUsedByTheseTraces: rate = (course.len - you.dist) < 200 ? 4.0 : 0; ease/launch/stumble false; tx = you.x; no shifting. NOTE this policy never steers and never brakes, which is fine for a conformance trace and NOT fine for judging difficulty (see docs/DEV-LOOP.md).

sampling.riderOrder: the order of race.riders, given per case as `riders`; index into d/v/e with it

tolerances.rule: Compare sample by sample and STOP AT THE FIRST MISMATCH. The first divergent sample is the bug; every later one is its echo. Report the frame, the rider and the field.
tolerances.whyNotExact: Different languages order floating point differently in a few places (Math.hypot, exponentiation). 1e-4 over a race is far tighter than any real behavioural difference and far looser than the last-bit noise.
